2608.26418.title: Redwood: A Frontier AI Accelerator Designed, Verified, and Deployed from Scratch in 2 Weeks by AI
2608.26418.paper_summary: Modern AI workloads and the hardware that runs them evolve on different timescales: architectural definition precedes volume silicon by years, while target workloads shift in months. Design decisions are therefore committed under deep uncertainty and paid for twice, once in the generality added as a hedge, and again when new workloads map poorly onto frozen silicon. As Moore's Law stagnates, specialization is the main remaining source of performance-per-watt and demands a design cycle that runs at the cadence of the workloads. We present an end-to-end AI system that collapses the software-to-silicon stack into a single optimization loop, where hardware and software are co-designed and verified under one objective. Its first demonstration is Redwood, a frontier AI accelerator built for single-batch, low-power, ultra-low-latency inference for physical AI. From a high-level specification by two human architects, the system autonomously generated the performance model, RTL design, UVM environments, formal proofs, firmware, and kernels in under two weeks with no human intervention below the specification. Every block reached 95% coverage via commercial EDA tools, our proprietary formal engine, and hardware-in-the-loop validation. Specification changes were reverified and redeployed to hardware in under 48 hours. Redwood Nano, its ultra-low-power FPGA variant, runs multi-billion-parameter models like Llama and Qwen. Projected onto Samsung 8 nm, the Jetson Orin Nano's process class, Redwood delivers 1.75x the throughput at 1.9x lower power, a 3.4x performance-per-watt gain against a measured Jetson baseline on the same models. Qwen running on Redwood also helped design next-generation Redwood, an early step toward recursive self-improvement. To our knowledge, this is the first production-worthy AI accelerator designed end-to-end by an AI system and running a modern AI model.
2608.26418.paper_summary_zh: 現代的人工智慧工作負載及其運行的硬體在不同的時間尺度上演變：架構定義比量產矽片早幾年，而目標工作負載則在幾個月內發生變化。因此，設計決策是在深度不確定性下做出的，並且付出了兩次代價，一次是作為對沖而增加的一般性，另一次是在新的工作負載與凍結的矽片不匹配時。隨著摩爾定律的停滯，專業化成為性能每瓦的主要來源，並要求設計週期與工作負載的節奏相符。我們提出了一個端到端的人工智慧系統，將軟體到矽片的堆疊壓縮為一個單一的優化迴圈，在這裡硬體和軟體在一個目標下共同設計和驗證。其首次演示是Redwood，一個為物理人工智慧設計的單批次、低功耗、超低延遲推理的前沿AI加速器。從兩位人類架構師的高階規範出發，該系統在不到兩週的時間內自主生成了性能模型、RTL設計、UVM環境、形式證明、韌體和內核，且在規範以下沒有任何人為干預。每個模塊通過商業EDA工具、我們的專有形式引擎和硬體在迴路驗證達到了95%的覆蓋率。規範變更在48小時內重新驗證並重新部署到硬體上。Redwood Nano，其超低功耗的FPGA變體，運行像Llama和Qwen這樣的多十億參數模型。在三星8納米、Jetson Orin Nano的製程類別上，Redwood在1.9倍更低功耗的情況下提供了1.75倍的吞吐量，對於在相同模型上測得的Jetson基準，性能每瓦增益達到3.4倍。在Redwood上運行的Qwen也幫助設計了下一代Redwood，這是邁向遞歸自我改進的早期步驟。據我們所知，這是第一個由人工智慧系統端到端設計並運行現代人工智慧模型的具生產價值的AI加速器。
2608.26418.author: Architect Labs et.al.
